replicated_originals.reference: Smith, S. M. et al. (2009) Correspondence of the brain's functional architecture during activation and rest. PNAS 106, 13040-13045

A.reason: Ref 27 (Smith et al. 2013, NeuroImage 80:144-168) is cited only as the description of the HCP resting-state data and its preprocessing, i.e. the data source for the replication.

B.reason: Ref 30; the paper explicitly sets out to replicate Smith et al. (2009) PNAS, reproducing its rest/task network correspondence (20- and 70-component ICA) with independent HCP task and resting-state fMRI data, and reports the findings were replicated.

notes: Uses the open HCP dataset (different participants and task data from Smith et al., who used BrainMap plus 36 resting-state subjects), so it is an independent-data replication, not a reanalysis of the original data. The network-activation-strength analysis (Figs 2-4) is described as novel, not a replication.
